areas_inspected: frontend/src/api.ts (API client, auth refresh flow, error handling)
frontend/src/auth.tsx (auth context, token management, single-flight refresh)
frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx (sidebar, header, CommandPalette, NotificationDropdown, ThemeToggle integration, hardcoded notifications)
frontend/src/components/ui.tsx (787 lines: Button, Input, Select, Modal, Form, Table, CommandPalette, NotificationDropdown, ThemeToggle, StatusBadge, etc.)
backend/internal/model/model.go (all Go structs, JSON tags, enums)
backend/internal/service/biz.go (asset, maintenance, master, user, dashboard services)

findings.title: Required Select validation silently fails — user sees no feedback when required location not picked
findings.why: Select renders a hidden proxy input (opacity:0, height:1px) with required=true for HTML5 validation. When user submits asset create form without picking a location, the browser blocks submit but shows no validation message because the proxy input is visually hidden. The onSubmit handler never fires, leaving user confused why nothing happens.
findings.evidence: ui.tsx lines 1969-1972: .select-proxy { opacity: 0; height: 1px; pointer-events: none; } — browser validates but cannot show UI. Assets.tsx line 232: <Select id="f-loc" required ...> for location on create.
findings.fix: Add custom required validation in the form submit handler (check form.location_id && form.category_id) and show inline error, or style .select-proxy to be focusable/visible when invalid (e.g., opacity:0 but position:absolute off-screen, not zero-size).

findings.title: Hardcoded demo notifications in production Layout — no API integration
findings.why: Layout.tsx lines 111-115 define a static notifs array with three fake NotificationItem objects. Comment on line 110 admits: "Notifikasi (data contoh; ganti dengan API)". This fake data renders in the NotificationDropdown for all users.
findings.evidence: Layout.tsx lines 111-115: const [notifs, setNotifs] = React.useState<NotificationItem[]>([{ id: '1', title: 'Aset baru ditambahkan', ... }]);
findings.fix: Replace with real API fetch: add useEffect to load notifications from an endpoint (e.g., GET /api/v1/notifications) and wire markAllRead / onClick to API calls. If endpoint doesn't exist yet, at minimum gate the demo data behind NODE_ENV !== 'production'.

findings.title: initPointerGlow() exported but never initialized — soft-glow effect on cards never runs
findings.why: fx.ts exports initPointerGlow() which adds a delegated pointermove listener to create a cursor-following glow on .card/.stat/.table-card/.promo elements. main.tsx imports theme.initTheme but does not import or call initPointerGlow(). The effect is completely dead code.
findings.evidence: fx.ts lines 3-16: export function initPointerGlow() { ... document.addEventListener('pointermove', ...) } — never invoked. main.tsx only calls initTheme().
findings.fix: Call initPointerGlow() in main.tsx after initTheme(), or remove the export if the feature is unwanted.

findings.title: CommandPortal lacks focus trap — Tab can escape the modal dialog
findings.why: CommandPalette renders via createPortal into document.body. Its onKeyDown handles Escape/Arrows/Enter but not Tab. Focus can leave the dialog into the page behind, violating ARIA dialog modality. No focus restoration on close either.
findings.evidence: ui.tsx lines 595-602: onKeyDown handles Escape, ArrowUp/Down, Home, End, Enter — no Tab handling. Layout.tsx line 229 renders <CommandPalette isOpen={cmdOpen} ... />.
findings.fix: Add focus trap in CommandPalette useEffect (when isOpen): capture Tab/Shift+Tab, cycle within focusable elements, and restore focus to trigger on close.

findings.title: NotificationDropdown onClick error leaves dropdown open
findings.why: NotificationDropdown item onClick handler: onClick={() => { item.onClick?.(); setOpen(false); }}. If item.onClick() throws, setOpen(false) never executes, leaving the dropdown stuck open.
findings.evidence: ui.tsx line 748: onClick={() => { item.onClick?.(); setOpen(false); }}. Layout.tsx passes notifItems with onClick that mutates state (line 118-119).
findings.fix: Wrap in try/finally: onClick={() => { try { item.onClick?.(); } finally { setOpen(false); } }}

findings.title: Select popover position not updated on scroll/resize — dropdown detaches from trigger
findings.why: Select calculates popover position once on open using trigger.getBoundingClientRect() and sets CSS variables (--st, --sl). The popover uses position:fixed. If user scrolls the page while the dropdown is open, the trigger moves but the popover stays fixed, visually detaching.
findings.evidence: ui.tsx lines 270-280: const r = trigger.getBoundingClientRect(); style={{ '--st': `${r.bottom}px`, '--sl': `${r.left}px` }}. No scroll/resize listener to recompute.
findings.fix: Add a scroll/resize listener on window/document when open that recomputes position, or close the dropdown on scroll (simpler).

findings.title: Asset create sends location_id as undefined when empty — backend expects valid UUID
findings.why: CreateAssetInput requires LocationID (valid UUID). Frontend payload: location_id: form.location_id || undefined. If user somehow bypasses required validation (see high finding #1), empty string becomes undefined → JSON omits key → Go decoder sets empty string → validation fails with RELASI_TIDAK_VALID.
findings.evidence: Assets.tsx line 90: location_id: form.location_id || undefined. biz.go CreateAssetInput line 205: LocationID string `json:"location_id"` — required by service validation line 210: if !model.IsUUID(in.LocationID) return RELASI_TIDAK_VALID.
findings.fix: Keep the required validation fix from finding #1. Additionally, ensure form.location_id defaults to a valid UUID or show clear error before submit.

findings.title: Asset update API does not support location change — frontend sends location_id but backend ignores it
findings.why: UpdateAssetInput (biz.go line 220) has fields: Nama, SerialNumber, CategoryID, PurchaseDate, Catatan — no LocationID. Frontend submit payload includes location_id: undefined (line 90). Backend ignores it. Users cannot move an asset to a different location via edit; they must use the separate Mutasi (movement) flow.
findings.evidence: biz.go lines 220-227: type UpdateAssetInput struct { Nama, SerialNumber, CategoryID, PurchaseDate, Catatan }. Assets.tsx line 90 includes location_id but it's not in backend input.
findings.fix: If location change on edit is desired, add LocationID to UpdateAssetInput and UpdateMeta repo call. If intentional, remove location_id from frontend payload to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Auth refresh: expired access token sent in Authorization header on refresh call — harmless but wasteful
findings.why: refreshAccessToken() calls apiFetch('/api/v1/auth/refresh', { method: 'POST' }). apiFetch adds Authorization: Bearer <expired_token> because accessToken is still in memory. Backend /auth/refresh is public (no auth middleware) and reads cookie only, so the header is ignored. No functional bug, but sends unnecessary header.
findings.evidence: auth.tsx line 83: await apiFetch('/api/v1/auth/refresh', { method: 'POST' }). api.ts line 48: if (accessToken) headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${accessToken}`. routes.go: /auth/refresh in public group.
findings.fix: In refreshAccessToken, call fetch directly without apiFetch wrapper, or temporarily clear accessToken before the call.

findings.title: Modal focus management: first focusable element may be hidden proxy input
findings.why: Modal useEffect (line 450) queries for first focusable: '.modal-body input:not(.select-proxy), .modal-body .select-trigger, ...'. It correctly excludes .select-proxy. Good. But if the first field is a Select, it focuses the .select-trigger (button), not the proxy input. This is correct behavior.
findings.evidence: ui.tsx line 450: querySelector excludes .select-proxy. Verified working as intended.
